aggregateToGenes

Source: R/aggregateToGenes.R
aggregateToGenes.Rd

Turns a per-region result into a per-gene table, through the links stored by annotateRegions. One row per gene, with the regions that reached it counted in each direction and the disagreement between them reported rather than resolved.

This is the table a conventional over-representation analysis needs, and the ranked list a gene-level GSEA needs, for the cases where the set level route of geneSetsToRegionSets and testRegionSets is not what is wanted. It is the weaker of the two routes and it is honest about why.

Usage

aggregateToGenes(
  results,
  method = "simes",
  decay = 5000,
  linkType = NULL,
  regionSets = NULL,
  adjustMethod = "BH",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

results

RegionSetDE.results object returned by testRegions, carrying links.

method

Character vector with what to compute, among "simes", which combines the p-values of the regions of a gene, and "potential", which sums their fold changes weighted by how plausible their links are. Default: "simes".

decay

Numeric value with the distance, in base pairs, at which the weight of a link falls to 1/e, used by "potential" when the links carry no weight of their own. Default: 5000.

linkType

Character vector with the kinds of link to follow, among "promoter" and "distal" as annotateRegions labelled them with its tssRegion. This is how the promoter-proximal and the distal table are built separately. Default: NULL, every link.

regionSets

Character vector with the names of the region sets the regions are taken from, which is the other way of restricting the table to one class of element, when the sets were already split at load time. Default: NULL, every set of the object.

adjustMethod

String with the multiple testing correction applied across the genes. Default: "BH".

verbose

Logical value to indicate whether the messages must be printed. Default: TRUE.

Value

A RegionSetDE.geneResults object. Its table, read with resultsTable, holds one row per gene:

  • gene.id, gene.symbol: the gene, and its symbol when the links carry one.

  • n.regions: how many regions of the object reached it.

  • n.up, n.down: how many of those are labelled "up" and "down" in the region table.

  • direction: "up" or "down" when the regions that changed agree, "mixed" when they do not, "unchanged" when none of them changed.

  • log2FC: the fold change of the region carrying the combined p-value, with "simes".

  • p.value, FDR: the Simes combination over the regions of the gene, corrected across the genes, with "simes".

  • score, score.magnitude: with "potential", the weighted sum of the fold changes of the regions of the gene, sum(w * log2FC), and the same sum on their absolute values, sum(w * abs(log2FC)).

Details

The reason this function exists alongside geneSetsToRegionSets, and the reason it is the second choice, is worth stating. Aggregating to genes throws away the ranking of the regions and replaces several measurements with one, which is exactly the step the set level route avoids. Use it when an external tool needs a gene table, when a reviewer asks for a conventional over-representation result, or when the gene rather than the region is genuinely the unit of the question. For asking which pathways responded, test the sets.

n.up and n.down are read from the diff.status column of the region table rather than recomputed, so they honour the FDR and log2FC the regions were labelled with, including after updateThresholds has changed them. The gene table therefore cannot disagree with the region table about what counts as up.

direction is the answer to the question that makes this whole exercise awkward. A gene reached by one region that opened and another that closed is "mixed", and nothing here decides which of the two wins, because there is no defensible way to decide it: cancelling them loses a real signal, and picking the stronger one is arbitrary. Treat the mixed genes as their own category rather than dropping them. They are where a rearranged regulatory landscape shows up, and a gene with three regions up and three down is a different biological statement from a gene with nothing happening, which a signed score cannot tell apart.

"simes" asks whether any region of the gene changed. It is relatively relaxed, valid under the positive dependence that regions of one locus have, and corrects for the number of regions a gene carries, which a minimum p-value does not. The fold change reported beside it belongs to the region that carried the p-value, not to an average, so a gene with one strong region among many quiet ones is described by that region.

"potential" is a score and not a test: it has no error model and no p-value of its own, which is why the Simes columns are worth keeping alongside it. For a gene reached by regions i carrying weights w[i], score is sum(w * log2FC) and score.magnitude is sum(w * abs(log2FC)). The first is signed, so a gene gaining at one region and losing at another lands near zero; the second ignores sign and does not, so the same gene scores high. Genes high in the second and near zero in the first are the rearranged ones, the same signal direction reports as a label.

score is the ranked gene-level statistic a GSEA takes, so fgsea::fgseaMultilevel(pathways = geneSets, stats = setNames(score, gene.id)) is the whole of that route; ranking on score.magnitude asks which sets were remodelled rather than which shifted, and sign(score) * -log10(p.value) ranks on significance rather than on effect. No wrapper for it is provided, since the call is one line and wrapping it would add a dependency without adding a decision. What does need stating in the methods is that the genes of the table are not independent, so the permutation behind any such test is anti-conservative.

The weights come from the links. A weight measured or predicted for the link itself is used as it is, whatever it measures, which is what weightSource in annotateRegions records. Failing that, the distance to the start site is turned into exp(-d / decay), which is a guess about contact rather than a measure of it. Failing both, every region of a gene counts the same. Which of the three applied is in the weighting slot and is printed by show.

Two things this does not fix, both worth a line in the methods. Genes are not independent here: a region linked to three genes contributes to all three, so the rows of the table share data and any test run on them afterwards is anti-conservative to an unquantified degree. And the number of regions a gene carries depends on the length of its regulatory locus, so a gene set rich in long-locus genes is easier to hit; a count-based method built for that bias, chipenrich or polyenrich, is the comparison to run when it matters.

A tiled result that was not combined back to regions is refused, since its rows are tiles and a gene would then be weighted by how finely its regions were cut. Test it with combine = TRUE first.

annotateRegions, geneSetsToRegionSets, testRegionSets, updateThresholds

Examples

counts <- loadExampleData("counts", verbose = FALSE)
fit <- loadExampleData("fit", verbose = FALSE)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes

# Links of your own, four regions per gene
regionTable <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowRanges(fit@counts))[, 1:3]
geneNumber <- ceiling(nrow(regionTable) / 4)

annotatedFit <- annotateRegions(fit,
                                linkTable = data.frame(regionTable,
                                                       gene.id = rep(paste0("gene", seq_len(geneNumber)),
                                                                     each = 4)[seq_len(nrow(regionTable))]),
                                verbose = FALSE)

results <- testRegions(annotatedFit, contrast = c("condition", "SHR", "BN"), verbose = FALSE)

geneResults <- aggregateToGenes(results, method = c("simes", "potential"), verbose = FALSE)
geneResults
#> An object of class 'RegionSetDE.geneResults'
#>   contrast        : condition: SHR vs BN 
#>   engine          : edgeR 
#>   aggregation     : simes, potential 
#>   weighting       : none 
#>   genes           : 474 
#>   links           : 1895 
#>   direction       : up 3, down 9, mixed 0, unchanged 462 
#> 
#>  gene.id gene.symbol n.regions n.up n.down direction score  p.value      FDR
#>   gene54        <NA>         4    0      1      down -6.55 4.59e-08 2.18e-05
#>  gene166        <NA>         4    0      1      down -1.88 1.10e-05 2.60e-03
#>    gene4        <NA>         4    0      1      down -4.22 5.48e-05 6.58e-03
#>  gene309        <NA>         4    0      1      down -5.30 5.55e-05 6.58e-03
#>  gene295        <NA>         4    0      1      down -2.18 1.34e-04 1.27e-02
#>  gene162        <NA>         4    1      0        up  9.27 1.68e-04 1.33e-02

geneTable <- resultsTable(geneResults)
table(geneTable$direction)
#> 
#>      down unchanged        up 
#>         9       462         3
